## 2026-08-19 — Keep EventSpikeSeg140k canonical and target digital neuromorphic FPGA inference

Canonical model naming is `EventSpikeSeg140k` for the ~140k deployment baseline and
`EventSpikeSegXL` for the optional 236,445-parameter expanded comparison. This naming
policy does not alter the trained canonical forward topology or parameters.

The canonical six-class model has 140,089 registered parameters, but its executed
inference graph uses 134,637. The inherited `refine2` block (5,056 parameters) is
registered but never called; the 396-parameter auxiliary head is training-only. FPGA
deployment targets the executed inference graph only.

The primary hardware direction is **custom VHDL-2008 on ZCU104**. PyTorch/SpikingJelly
remains the training and floating-point golden-reference stack. Convolution kernels are
shared synaptic weights/connectivity; PLIF feature-map elements are logical neuron states.
FPGA inference represents weights, membrane/current, beta, thresholds, and adaptation
with deterministic fixed-point numbers rather than physical voltages/currents.

The hardware should stay as neuromorphic as practical despite being fully digital:
inter-layer communication is binary spikes/events, active spike addresses trigger shared
weight additions, PLIF state persists in banked memory, and inactivity-aware scheduling
should suppress unnecessary work. The baseline preserves learned per-channel beta with a
quantized coefficient; shift-only/power-of-two leakage is an optimization only if
bit-level behavior and semantic accuracy are revalidated.

Scale is handled with reusable coarse-grained synaptic-accumulator + PLIF processing
elements, not one datapath per logical neuron. The same PEs are time-multiplexed across
spatial tiles/channels/stages while membrane/adaptation state remains in BRAM/URAM/
LUTRAM. Start with exact full/tiled execution, then consider touched-address lists,
active-neuron lists, lazy decay, and clock-enable optimizations.

Nontrivial RTL items are the stem peer-membrane inhibition rule, triangular threshold
adaptation, and the selector's global binary channel enable. The selector `amax(H,W)` can
be implemented efficiently as a per-channel any-spike flag because selector outputs are
binary. Do not silently remove any of these mechanisms; approximations require
revalidation/fine-tuning.

Verification proceeds from SpikingJelly float to a bit-exact integer reference, VHDL RTL
simulation, Vivado synthesis/place-and-route, post-implementation timing simulation, and
representative-event SAIF/VCD power analysis. These Vivado results are estimates. Only
instrumented ZCU104 results may be called measured hardware power/latency.

## 2026-08-20 — Separate shared parameters from per-neuron runtime state for FPGA mapping

Do not use the ~140k parameter count as a proxy for logical PLIF state. Convolution weights
are spatially shared and beta/base threshold are shared per output channel, but every
executed PLIF output element `(layer,c,y,x)` retains its own membrane value. Summing the
37 inference PLIF populations gives `N_mem = (672+Nclass)HW + 480H2W2 + 1280H4W4`.
Corrected for `project2` executing before upsample, six-class DDD17 at 212x282 has
**51,089,456 independent membrane states**.

The threshold-adaptation-enabled scopes contain `352H2W2 + 1216H4W4` logical neurons, or **9,836,800**
at 212x282; each carries adaptation age and adaptation amplitude. These persistent states
are distinct from temporary synaptic-current accumulation and from sparse spike-event FIFOs.

FPGA execution should therefore keep weights/kernel connectivity static/shared while
virtualizing logical neuron state in addressable memory. A small physical PLIF PE array may
be reused across layers and spatial positions, but different logical neuron addresses must
never share one stored membrane value. For exact equivalence, all synaptic contributions for
a layer/timestep are accumulated first, then each PLIF is updated/thresholded once. Hidden
spikes may be processed input-centrically as `(c,y,x)` addresses, so dense sliding-window
convolution is not required. Lazy decay/touched-neuron-only updates remain later
optimizations because they change when decay is evaluated and must be proven equivalent
with reset, peer-membrane inhibition, and triangular threshold adaptation.

## 2026-08-21 — Preserve DSEC event density and supervise complete records

The original DSEC scheduler collapsed every repeated `(clock, polarity, y, x)` event to
one, discarding local event density. It also applied the complete semantic mask to each
temporal chunk independently, so the five-chunk profile imposed the same final target on
five partial 10 ms histories. Replace the external event value with
`min(log2(count + 1), 4)`, retaining unit value for a single event while compressing and
bounding bursts. Hidden inter-layer communication remains binary.

Retain all ten chronological 5 ms clocks but combine their time-normalized logits before
computing weighted CE, present-class Dice, and auxiliary CE. Each 50 ms record now yields
one semantic objective. Numeric membrane/adaptation state continues across consecutive
records and is reset only at epoch, validation, sequence, or frame-gap boundaries.
Chunking remains available for state-carry execution, but its outputs contribute to the
same full-window objective; the compose profiles use one chunk because exact nonlinear
full-window loss must retain the output graphs until backward.

This changes the DSEC temporal protocol to `dsec-log-count-events-full-window-v2`, so old
binary/partial-loss checkpoints are intentionally incompatible. EventSpikeSeg140k remains
the canonical deployment model; EventSpikeSegXL is an explicitly named comparison run.

## 2026-08-21 — Make DSEC deployment asynchronous and training timestamp-aware (superseded 2026-08-22)

The bounded-log/full-window decision above still described a clocked input model and is
superseded for DSEC. The final FPGA must accept sequential camera events directly; it must
not store 5 ms input bins or run a global neural timestep. Each touched neuron stores a
last-update timestamp, applies `beta ** (delta_us / 5000)`, receives the shared synaptic
weight, thresholds/resets, and immediately enqueues generated binary spikes. State carries
across semantic labels and resets only at sequence/frame gaps.

PyTorch/SpikingJelly remains the fast training backend. It accumulates chronological
source events into `internal_updates` fixed physical-time divisions, preserves linear
event multiplicity without log/cap, and supplies the fixed elapsed duration to the same
physical-time neuron equation. Event density never changes the number of training updates.
These divisions are a training approximation, not an FPGA input representation.

All packets in the 50 ms label interval contribute to one final semantic objective. For
memory-bounded XL training, first form the complete-record prediction without retaining
activation graphs, then restore initial neuron state and replay chronological chunks using
the one objective's output gradients. Keep the replay snapshot in host RAM to avoid a
second full persistent-state copy on the GPU. This is truncated state-gradient history,
but it is not multiple partial-history target losses. Logits/rates are normalized by
elapsed physical time so packet count does not change their scale.

The global spatial selector gate is incompatible with immediate event propagation. Replace
its `amax(H,W)` channel enable with a local retinotopic 1x1-PLIF binary gate. The new DSEC
protocol is `dsec-fixed-time-counts-async-fpga-v4`; older checkpoints are rejected.

Promote `EventSpikeSegXL` from an undocumented capacity comparison to the active detailed
implementation target for the 11-class DSEC configuration at `241x351`. Retain

## 2026-08-22 — Use 50 ms record-level, T=10 fixed-step FPGA inference

DSEC still starts from exact raw `(t,x,y,p)` events, but both software training and baseline FPGA inference assign every event to one of ten chronological 5 ms slices inside the 50 ms semantic interval. Event multiplicity is preserved. The network therefore executes ten fixed PLIF updates per record and emits one segmentation result after temporal class-spike counting over the complete 50 ms interval.

The FPGA scheduling order is intentionally **layer-major over the complete T=10 record**. For layer `L`, process slices `t0..t9` sequentially using that layer's own persistent membrane/adaptation state, buffer its ten output spike slices, then let layer `L+1` consume that sequence. This is equivalent to the trained multi-step feed-forward graph because recurrent state is local to each PLIF population.

This scheduling choice is also the baseline state-memory strategy. Load a layer/state tile once, keep it resident while executing all ten 5 ms updates, and write its final state back after `t9`. Sparse event-address convolution remains enabled within each slice, so zero spike locations do not trigger synaptic additions. The baseline explicitly advances every required state in known 5 ms steps and therefore does not require a 32-bit `last_update_us` field per membrane. Timestamp/lazy-decay storage becomes an optional later optimization only if the integer reference proves exact equivalence.

The runtime is **not fully asynchronous**. The real-time throughput target is one complete 50 ms record every 50 ms (20 Hz); record acquisition and compute may be double-buffered. The ten internal 5 ms steps may not be collapsed into a single 50 ms PLIF update.

## 2026-08-23 — Stream live DSEC in 5 ms bins and preserve touched-neuron lazy state

This supersedes the same-day 50 ms layer-major FPGA scheduling decision while leaving training unchanged. Live camera events are accumulated into consecutive 5 ms ON/OFF bins. One sealed bin must traverse the full deployed graph (27 PLIF actors plus the stateless class-current update) before the bin is retired. Input uses ping-pong buffers so bin `k+1` is captured while bin `k` computes.

The current DSEC training path enables touched-neuron lazy updates. Runtime must therefore preserve that behavior: each live sparse neuron state stores a compact 24-bit `last_bin_tag`; when touched at bin `k`, compute `delta_bins = k - last_bin_tag (mod 2^24)` and apply the learned beta once per elapsed bin before adding current. The first RTL implementation uses an iterative beta multiply so long-idle neurons consume additional cycles; a beta-power LUT/accelerator is allowed later only with bit-exact validation. No 32-bit microsecond timestamp is used.

polarity 0 is red (negative), polarity 1 is blue (positive), and a shared logarithmic
count scale controls intensity so both low- and high-count pixels remain visible.

The signed 16->11 class-current readout accumulates over a configurable prediction window. Start with ten bins, therefore one prediction every 50 ms / 20 Hz, because that matches training. PLIF/adaptation state continues across prediction boundaries and resets only at sequence/frame gaps.

Define real-time utilization `U = C_bin / (f_clk * 5 ms)` and throughput headroom `H = 1/U`. Sustained operation requires `U <= 1` (`H >= 1`). The starting engineering target is `U <= 0.8` (`H >= 1.25`), leaving 20% timing margin. At 100/150/200 MHz the hard budgets are 500k/750k/1M cycles per bin and the 80% target budgets are 400k/600k/800k cycles. These values must come from measured controller cycle counts after synthesis/RTL integration, not from parameter count.

## 2026-08-25 — Use native SystemVerilog and sequential raw-event ASIC ingress

This supersedes the VHDL/GHDL portion and the ping-pong-bin ingress portion of the preceding

Icarus/cocotb, Yosys, and OpenROAD. Preserve the FPGA attempt in the non-normative

The ASIC camera interface accepts rectified raw events sequentially in timestamp order.
Each event immediately triggers only its connected static-weight additions; it does not
load a dense 5 ms tensor and does not fetch or update unrelated neuron state. A completion
token is inserted at each trained 5 ms boundary. That token causes each actor to commit
only its touched PLIF destinations once, emit spikes, and forward completion.

Do not threshold or reset a PLIF after every individual signed contribution. Training
performs one PLIF update per 5 ms division after convolutional accumulation, and signed
kernel contributions can cancel. Immediate per-event firing would therefore be a different
event-time neuron model and would require explicit event-driven retraining and accuracy
validation. The current ASIC is sparse and event-sequential in its synaptic work while
retaining the trained 5 ms PLIF commit semantics.

## 2026-08-25 — Treat the 25 ASIC actors as the exact v8 DAG, never as a linear pipeline

`EventSpikeSeg140k` deploys 25 PLIF populations, but their enumeration is only a stable
topological/export order. Runtime interconnect must reproduce the actual model DAG. Input
events fork into `detail_stem` and `stem`; residual blocks binary-OR their bypass and main
spikes; `x1` and `x2` fan out into deeper encoder and later decoder routes; `project3` and
`project2` use 2x nearest-event fanout; decoder concatenations use fixed channel remapping;
`project2 + x1` deliberately preserves coincident events as multiplicity two; semantic and
detail routes converge before `final_fuse.standard`.

Completion tokens follow the same directed routes. A fanout duplicates the tagged token to
every required branch. A multi-input residual/skip/concat node may emit one downstream
completion only after all required upstream tokens for the same 5 ms bin have arrived. This
rendezvous rule is required for correctness: a fast branch must not close a downstream PLIF
epoch before a slower skip/detail branch has contributed.

Use compile-time dedicated routing rather than a programmable NoC unless later evidence
shows programmability is worth its area/energy cost. Actor-local membrane/adaptation SRAM
remains unchanged by this decision; only spikes and completion tokens traverse the graph.

semantics. Keep depth compile-time configurable and measure native occupancy before replacing the

Treat busiest-bank service interval and same-bin response latency as separate acceptance gates.

choose a candidate, but its projection is never reported as measured latency.

For inhibition/adaptation actors, distinguish accumulation ownership from commit ownership.
Synaptic currents and persistent per-channel PLIF state may use independent channel-by-spatial SRAM

addition order within that bank, and must drain before the actor accepts the bin completion token.

The final direct-state ASIC uses register/latch-resident current, membrane, and enabled adaptation
state for every logical PLIF neuron; it does not use an addressed state SRAM or touched-address

The inter-actor representation for this implementation is a binary spike vector per PLIF
population and bin. Static convolutional synapses are compile-time wires/constants that reduce
the asserted presynaptic bits into a signed current delta for every destination in parallel.
More than one accepted vector transaction in a bin adds the delta again, preserving multiplicity

the 24-bit bin tag. This removes the scalar per-channel contribution bottleneck as well as the
addressed state fetch, at the explicit cost of wide routing and replicated adder logic.

Wide fanout must not silently allocate a second full feature-map register bank. The resident

has accepted it. Residual branches rendezvous and OR complete binary vectors; concatenation
remaps fixed channel slices; the half-resolution decoder sum forwards both vector pulses before
completion so coincident activity causes two downstream additions. Raw ingress remains scalar
and is decoded into a one-hot pulse independently at each first-layer branch.

# 2026-09-24 — switched-capacitor path remains active; resolve small-weight floor

The active analog reference is the ordinary best-validation float32 checkpoint; quantized/QAT values are not required for an analog design. The switched-capacitor MOS virtual-summing-node cell remains the active exploration path, but the physical state interface is failing. Corrected baseline-subtracted packet curves are monotonic in both signs, while the full-float software sensitivity still leaves 26.1–54.6% of final-fusion weights below the measured floor. Direct TG initialization produces 0.259–0.326V state error; a held-output variant produces 0.050–0.117V error, and a coarse 3×3 plus fine 4×2 bias sweep has no acceptable combination of state accuracy and hold drift: the best state match drifts 49mV and the least-drift point misses state by 62mV. Those packet curves and output agreements do not qualify the hardware. Next debug the OTA output equilibrium and state isolation, then return to offset correction and full-float mapping.

## 2026-09-24 — matched reference cancels nominal reconnect common mode

Keep the full-float trained checkpoint as the analog reference; QAT and quantized exports do not set analog precision. The late-switched VCM-referenced readout works across event orders in TT, but its fixed gain varies across process corners: gain 1.0 is accurate in TT/FF and misses SS by 17.37µV; gain 1.35 corrects SS but over-gains TT by 21.49µV. The OTA input-size sweep did not find a shared solution. Its 1GΩ input/feedback network is also idealized and lacks physical resistor geometry. ## 2026-09-25 — readout direction: active differential sensing

The passive MIM sampler is not the preferred readout: reducing its size leaves estimated kT/C above the event signal, while enlarging it approaches the signal scale only by adding membrane loading; nominal feedthrough also requires an unimplemented baseline correction. Keep the passive sampler only as a comparator/control. Noise, PVT, mismatch and physical implementation remain open.

An idealized software first-touch clamp largely removes the two-frame mean-IoU collapse seen when independent reset noise is imposed on every state at record initialization. It does not establish hardware feasibility or model fidelity across the validation set. A physical SKY13010µm MIM/TG/MOS timing screen shows that the clamp must open before the injector turns on:0.2–10ns lead gives the reference≈16.68µV retained contribution, simultaneous opening gives≈157µV, and1ns late gives≈3.22mV. Use this as a provisional local two-phase ordering requirement. Next qualify switch thermal noise, process/temperature/mismatch timing, untouched-state retention, first-touch detection and full-population event throughput. Reject the per-state OTA/output-MIM baseline sampler; keep layout and architecture acceptance gated.

Selected SS/FF MOS corners at0/85°C leave the release-order condition intact but vary the same fixed-gate event contribution37.3× (3.77–140.59µV). The next analog circuit choice must include a stable or calibrated charge-per-event source; do not treat nominal fixed-gate mapping as a qualified weight encoding.

First-touch also does not remove the resident-state area gate. Do not select a sparse exact-zero analog state pool on the current evidence. A one-local-cap plus ideal shared-reference proxy halves bare MIM area and improves first-touch replay over an independent pair, but a10µm capacitor still costs3,097.6mm² across the full inventory, while5µm loses mean IoU on both sampled frames. Do not assume one scalar PVT gain trim fixes the fixed-width MOS weight encoding. ## Charge-bucket reference decision — 2026-09-30

Do not select the continuous single-ended OTA integrator with a separate zero-charge OTA reference for the low-microvolt PLIF readout. ## State representation direction — 2026-09-30

Do not choose a fixed linear gain and hard clamp for the full-float membrane. On two complete records, an optimistic per-record32–64× range compression plus independent10µm-pair Gaussian reset-noise proxy still changes4.6–4.9% of final-fusion spikes and about20–22% of pixel classes;100× gain makes roughly14% of spikes and more than half of pixels disagree. Higher gain reduces input-referred noise but clips accumulated state. Keep the analog research direction: evaluate a *specific* nonlinear or split-range state representation with shared differential common-mode/offset control, then validate a physical state store and actual weighted-event/reset behavior. This is a research direction, not a selected circuit or evidence for QAT/digital fallback.

The ideal `asinh` state bound improves this software tradeoff but is not a design selection. Its mathematical inverse preserves the zero-noise float trajectory; at about1010× near-zero voltage gain the10µm-pair noise proxy still changes2.31/2.41% of final-fusion spikes and12–13% of pixel classes on two records. It requires a state-dependent signed event transformation absent from the current additive MOS injector, plus physical analog storage, threshold and reset. Explore a realizable split-range/charge-domain mechanism before selecting any nonlinear state macro. No QAT or digital model switch.

Use an eight-range piecewise state-voltage map as the next **physical feasibility target**, not a selected macro. It approximates the ideal compander in a two-frame software noise screen, but would require~4,496× gain span and charge-preserving transitions across segment boundaries. Prove one signed boundary-crossing event and held state in a bounded SKY130 circuit before any macro, area or full-neuron claim. If that physical mechanism fails, return to another analog state representation without changing the trained float model.
The first positive boundary-crossing bench passed only with ideal matched precharge, manual timing and ideal current, while its5ms hold decayed. Therefore the physical gate remains reverse crossing with an actual weighted source, programmable boundary reference, and retention/noise; the conditional positive result cannot select a macro.

The complete eight-range *per-state capacitance bank* is ruled out by the conditional~28.9m² bare-MIM area calculation. Prioritize state-dependent signed event-charge generation on a modest analog store or a shared active integrator. The actual max-fanin float-event demand reaches342mV for one ideal encoded update and5–22 events per examined order exceed the existing16.624mV single-event bank calibration, so the linear direct-MOS event lookup cannot simply be reused unchanged. Physical event subdivision, state sensing/control, reverse range crossing and hold/noise still require evidence; the eight-range map remains a software bound.

The bank-loaded ten-pulse screen makes state-dependent signed balance a required gate for the direct-MOS branch. Equal positive and negative pulses cancel almost exactly at zero stored differential but leave~0.131mV residual at±0.6V. Do not extrapolate a zero-state gate map to biased high-cancellation paths; the next physical source candidate needs state-aware polarity compensation or another differential charge-balancing mechanism.

Manual polarity-specific ideal gate bias restores nominal ten-pulse cancellation to≤0.6µV at the two screened±0.6V states. Keep state-aware polarity correction as a plausible analog research path. It cannot be selected until a physical sensing/programming loop, interpolated state law, actual mixed float weights, noise/mismatch and5ms service are demonstrated.

The actual mixed float-weight physical fan-in now narrows that path: ideal first-segment gain produces a good23.699mV near-threshold sum, but a separate+5.442µV high-cancellation target has up to67.089µV signed error and a shuffled sign reversal. Reusing the equal-pulse state/polarity coefficient across mixed weights only partly helps. Do not select the fixed zero-state MOS lookup or its one-geometry polarity correction as a precise companded injector; require a measured weight/geometry/state calibration and physical controller, then repeat the full signed fan-in and noise/hold gates.

The high-cancellation prefix screen locates~20µV signed error by event120 while the event mix spans all13 geometries and a broad bias range. Treat that as an injector transfer-calibration problem, but keep independent-state noise, retention and population area as parallel feasibility gates. Do not spend layout effort on a locally calibrated injector before the state representation has a credible physical storage and readout path.

The first physical range-switch screen does not clear that target. Ideal boundary-matched extension preparation allows a manually timed positive current event to cross one boundary with0.177mV immediate state error, but the actual precharge source and range detector are absent. A VCM-precharged extension loses~71.5mV of the intended112.5mV state at connection. Even with matched ideal preparation, the event difference decays6.82% over5ms. Prefer testing a **shared fixed boundary reference** for extension precharge before designing per-state tracking buffers. At an exact known segment boundary, the extension target is fixed; a deterministic±1mV reference perturbation moves the positive-crossing final state by about±0.635mV. This is a source-calibration and connection-timing requirement, not proof of feasible distribution or mismatch tolerance. The physical reference/programming circuit and range detector remain absent; this refinement does not accept the macro.

Reject the full-range **per-state switched-capacitance bank** implied by the ideal eight-range voltage map. Holding event charge per model unit fixed would require~933pF per side in its final segment,~683µm square SKY130 MIMs and~28.9m² bare two-cap area for30.976m logical states. The one-boundary TG/MIM bench remains useful for switching physics, but should not be replicated as an eight-range store. Retain the nonlinear software result only as a target for state-dependent event-charge control or shared active integration on a smaller store; neither has passed a physical circuit or model replay with measured errors. Analog full float remains the reference.
## MOS gate storage remains diagnostic — 2026-10-01

A bounded SKY130 TT screen gives3.14–3.84× the MIM capacitance at equal100µm² drawn gate area, but physical-TG off-center 5ms hold drifts3.7–4.6mV and an independent differential pair still has a102–113µV kT/C proxy. The immediate refresh follow-up shows why a **simple per-state refresh sweep** should not proceed to layout: the nominal drift implies millions of parallel 1µs refresh channels under an illustrative3µV error bound, and a single exponential leakage calibration misses intermediate states by22–258µV in one TT5ms screen. A smarter analog state representation or physically measured state-dependent correction is required. These conditional probes do not prove every analog state store impossible; the full-float analog path remains active.

Do not lay out the tested two-TG stacked MOS state store. Adding up to a10µm middle-node MIM does not reduce the3.7–4.6mV5ms drift. Ideal-initialized bare storage has zero nominal drift, while the off NFET/PFET attached to it create opposing millivolt leakage. Continue device/bias topology research or a separately justified analog state representation before any macro selection.

Do not choose the tested body-to-state switch bias. Its largest simulated movements occur outside or at the documented device body-bias range, while the in-range single-device cases still move millivolts and have no isolated-well layout. The special SkyWater SRAM pass devices are hard-IP-restricted, so their name is not grounds for a custom analog switch claim. No MOS state-store macro is selected; module/layout/full-chip readiness remains false.

The official public SKY1305V-gate NFET/PFET models give essentially the same sampled MOS state drift as the installed1.8V TG at the tested TT points. Do not select a simple thick-oxide substitution for layout. Continue to seek a physically supported state representation that passes signed update, 5ms retention, noise and population service together; original full-float analog remains the target.

The new full-float two-frame replay demotes the **linear small-MOS state cell under independent reset noise**: a113µV kT/C-scale proxy plus measured TT hold drift gives13.7% final-fusion spike mismatch and mean IoU~0.119 against float~0.20. Keep the original full-float analog direction and research a state-dependent charge/sense circuit; do not lay out either candidate as a completed PLIF cell. The software results do not prove dataset accuracy or physical noise yield.

This does not demonstrate accurate state initialization or complete neural updates.

Native NF0.5um/L1um and 7um MIM are schematic; write/select/park TGs and clock inverters use qualified cap-extracted components. Ideal shared 1.65V column clamp and zero-drain parking remain bench assumptions. Zero parking avoids the modeled continuous sense-channel DC path; leakage, noise, mismatch, PVT, finite array loading and standby power remain unqualified. No sense-cell layout or new physical acceptance. All launched runs completed.

Alternatives: (1) non-destructive current read with shared column electronics is the next candidate; (2) local switched-capacitor updates can apply learned beta once per bin, signed weighted accumulation, threshold and subtractive reset in place, but require area/noise evaluation; (3) calibrated destructive read/restore remains a fallback with nonlinear inverse and switch-error burden. Uncontrolled continuous-time leakage is not a substitute for the trained bin equation. A switched-capacitor neuromorphic implementation is documented at https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3233; it establishes precedent, not feasibility for this population.

Next milestone: implement and characterize the sense cell and a real shared column frontend, reduce initial-write error, then integrate one complete analog PLIF neuron preserving the original float model equations. Evaluate model tolerance, 5ms population service and realistic area before full-chip assembly/layout. No QAT/digital fallback. ## ASAP7 MOSCAP bounded qualification — 2026-09-23

After correcting D-G-S-B wiring and leakage-subtracted Ceff analysis, the complete small-count Docker rerun (`python scripts/test_asap7_mos_storage.py --only all`) completed all three benches. Four-finger C-V median is 0.27035 fF total (0.06759 fF/finger). Eight-finger write/drain/rewrite passes its bounded voltage checks. Eight-finger MOSCAP retention from 0.41969 V to 0.22255 V over 5.002 ms drifts −0.19714 V (−2.816 model units), failing the provisional 0.02-unit limit by a wide margin. Therefore `accepted_as_option_b_candidate=false`; drain/adjust success does not qualify storage. No sizing, layout or ORFS work is authorized by this result. Next work is to diagnose/redesign the storage and hold path, then repeat multi-condition 5 ms validation before scaling. Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/asap7/capacitor_qualification.json`, `results/mos_storage_checks.json`, and the three bench logs/traces.

### Retention isolation follow-up

`python scripts/diagnose_asap7_mos_retention.py` ran bounded Docker controls with the same transmission-gate stimulus. The sub-fF ideal-cap control (8× measured nMOS per-finger Ceff) drifted −0.2260 V; 1pF and 20pF ideal controls drifted −0.01514 V and −0.000804 V respectively. Eight- and 32-finger nMOS Cgg drifted −0.17675 V and −0.13992 V. An 8-finger pMOS Cgg cell improved drift to −0.01094 V (−0.156 model units), still 7.8× beyond the ±0.02-unit smoke gate; 32- and 128-finger pMOS arrays drifted +0.04154 V and +0.15020 V. Rail current on the common-mode/reference rail is in `results/mos_retention_diagnosis.json`; these are schematic diagnostics, not a physical design. Floating-node runs are invalid controls because ngspice initialized the state near 0.77 V rather than the requested 0.42 V. No tested ASAP7 MOS Cgg option qualifies. Continue analog-only debugging; digital/XL stay paused unless the user explicitly requests a switch. A later pMOS interior-bias trace that appeared stable at one endpoint was an input-dependent attracting equilibrium, not retention: high initial states drifted 68–145mV in adversarial cases. The DC bias map found minimum pMOS storage clamp current 6.787pA at stored 0.28V, versus an approximate 0.328fA budget for 1.17fF and 1.4mV/5ms. Direct OSDI `IGTOT` at 0.28V measured −0.9265pA for one pMOS instance (≈−7.412pA for eight), confirming modeled gate current as the dominant low-state branch rather than current-print quantization. A bounded low-common-mode nMOS-only screen used state 0.08/0.15/0.22V, eight NFIN=3 storage instances tied D/S/B=0, and one nMOS access path. Standalone AC admittance measured Cdiff=0.5415/0.5439/0.5756fF; summed intrinsic gate leakage corresponds to 0.124/0.413/0.822V/s, passing the provisional 0.28V/s rate only at the lowest state. The six state/input DC combinations also include access-current cases exceeding the rate limit (worst ≈4.03V/s). This low-common-mode diagnostic is not the project PLIF encoding and is not a hold-cell pass. The open ASAP7 files/survey contain no discrete MIM/MOM device model or PCell; do not invent a capacitor model or physical density. Readiness correctly remains false with `capacitor_qualification_candidate_not_accepted`. Diagnostic artifacts: `results/low_common_mode_nmos_only_dc.log`, `results/nmos_cap_standalone_ac_*.dat`, `results/mos_cap_igtot_bias_survey.json`, and `results/mos_off_bias_reachability.json`.

### Event-order collection timing rejected the spatial-only mechanism datapath

- instrumented exact event order, same-cycle scatter replacement, ordinary three-cycle bank
  cadence, mechanism five-cycle cadence plus first-spatial-touch write, and completion admission
  only after every bank returns to collect;
- the promoted 924-lane mapping fails before inter-actor FIFOs are considered. `down2.standard`
  requires 40,097,168 collection cycles and 40,107,810 cycles including its busiest commit bank
  (200.539 ms at 200 MHz); `stem` needs 6,593,614 total isolated cycles;
- `final_fuse.standard` also rises from its bank-count floor to 1,875,150 isolated cycles because a
  single pending-event bitmap stalls all otherwise independent banks when any destination bank is
  busy;
- the mechanism failure is structural: spatial-only contribution ports serialize all output
  channels that target the same pixel. More spatial modulo banks cannot fix this same-pixel
  serialization;
- next resume point: separate mechanism accumulation banking from mechanism commit atomicity.
  Channel-by-spatial current/state ports must collect independently, then one spatial coordinator
  must read peer channels, apply inhibition/adaptation atomically, and write them together. Ordinary
  actors also need multiple pending scatter contexts or per-bank projection queues.

# 2026-09-24 — corrected full-float mapping and packet-floor sensitivity

The mapped parameter archive already folds ChannelAffine into `weight__*`; the earlier screen multiplied that gain twice. Corrected the screen and retained the true checkpoint/runtime-gain replay. With only final_fuse remapped through the baseline-corrected cap-area curve and sub-1µm responses dropped, the three-patch full-graph software sensitivity is 91.87–94.17% pixel argmax agreement and 2.55–5.28% final_fuse spike-bit mismatch across 0.6–0.15V headroom. No task accuracy or analog qualification follows. Matched same-phase no-event subtraction removes a ~7.38µV startup/feedthrough offset; both packet signs are monotonic from 5–300mV and magnitude mismatch drops from 35.8% at 5mV to 0.69% at 300mV. The 0.25–10µm corrected geometry curve is monotonic for both signs, though sub-1µm physical legality remains unproven. The later physical sequence reported below supersedes the earlier init-failure conclusion. Active candidate remains SC virtual-ground charge integration; no QAT/quantized weights are involved.

## 2026-09-24 — physical SC init, retention and packet ordering

Fixed the held-integrator bench sequence after tracing two setup errors: the original init pulse overlapped OTA reconnection, and the short nonoverlap pulse did not allow the large 100×100µm² membrane capacitor to settle. A 2.5µs TG init pulse followed by a 0.5µs guard initializes 0.75/0.90/1.05V states within 109µV. With OTA and packet switches held off, the state changes by no more than 0.247mV over 5ms. After that hold, reconnecting the OTA and applying a ±0.3V top-plate packet on the 1µm packet capacitor gives corrected signed state increments −41.0…−41.3µV / +41.1…+41.2µV across the three states. The 10µm diagnostic gives ±3.102mV. Packet bottom and OTA switches must open before the top plate returns to VCM; returning the top plate while the packet remains connected cancels its integrated charge. The bench artifacts are `sky130_sc_packet_state_sweep.json`, `sky130_sc_physical_retention_sweep.json`, and `sky130_sc_physical_retention_packet_sweep.json`. This is nominal TT schematic evidence only; no PVT, mismatch, noise, extracted parasitics, physical MIM legality or float-model accuracy is established. Next: repeated signed packets, order sensitivity, reset and short float-trace sensitivity with the corrected phase order.

## 2026-09-24 — physical two-packet reset reuse

The physical held-output cell now has a repeatable two-packet sequence with transistor TG state init, packet-cap reset between events, and disconnect-before-top-plate-return phase ordering. Across four sign sequences (`pp`, `nn`, `pn`, `np`) and initial states 0.75/0.90/1.05V, same-sign sums are about ±82µV, mixed-sign residuals ≤0.43µV, max error against the two single-packet reference steps 0.621µV, and `pn`/`np` order difference 0.075µV. Physical init remains within 109µV. This is only a short-interval TT schematic screen; realistic packet spacing within a 5ms bin remains the next check. Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_sc_physical_accumulation.json`.

## 2026-09-24 — 5ms-spaced packet sequence and OTA reconnect kick

A physical-init two-packet test spaced events at 0.5ms and 4.5ms. The first-event contribution drifts ≤0.56µV relative to a same-phase no-event cell over the intervening ~4ms hold; final same-sign accumulation is −65.32/+65.27µV versus an ±82.30µV reference (17.03µV max error), and `pn`/`np` differ by 4.20µV. The no-event path shifts by −15.67mV across the two OTA reconnect windows, so the corrected charge result depends on a simulator control that does not exist in the circuit. The post-packet settle tail lowers hold drift but increases accumulation error; OTA bias sleep lowers hold drift to 0.24µV but leaves −14.64mV common shift; a 0.5µs soft-start of both bias rails improves hold drift to 0.10µV but leaves −14.54mV common shift and 16.90µV accumulation error; OTA-output precharge variants destabilize the state (−711.7mV and −890.36mV common shifts). These variants do not solve the reconnect kick.

The physical ±41.16µV 1µm packet measurement was used to anchor the cap-floor replay on the full-float 140k best checkpoint and the same three real DSEC training patches. Final_fuse spike mismatch is 5.325/3.947/2.605% and pixel argmax agreement is 91.805/93.319/94.092% at 0.15/0.30/0.60V candidate headroom. This remains local software sensitivity, not model accuracy or a complete analog inference. Next investigate a reconnect topology with a physical common-mode correction path. Reports: `sky130_sc_physical_long_bin_accumulation.json`, `sky130_sc_physical_long_bin_sleep_accumulation.json`, `sky130_sc_physical_long_bin_precharge_accumulation.json`, `sky130_sc_physical_long_bin_sleep_precharge_accumulation.json`, and `model_reference/float_patch_trace.json`.

The old 100ns near-zero-kick result was timestep-dependent. Direct paired-reference sign sensing is not accepted. ## 2026-10-08 — Method change: non-destructive current sensing selected for investigation

Overall stage: analog block validation, before complete PLIF integration. The destructive charge-read/capture/inverse/rewrite path remains unaccepted; repeated switch tuning has not removed its millivolt errors. Suspend further dummy-sizing sweeps and prioritize a small resident sense transistor with shared column readout, keeping membrane charge in its capacitor. Temporary read coupling is 1.47–8.11mV and initial write-release error remains 16.81–33.41mV. Read currents are monotonic at these three points, but nonlinear; no implemented decoder/calibration. This does not demonstrate accurate state initialization or complete neural updates.

Native NF0.5um/L1um and 7um MIM are schematic; write/select/park TGs and clock inverters use qualified cap-extracted components. Ideal shared 1.65V column clamp and zero-drain parking remain bench assumptions. Zero parking avoids the modeled continuous sense-channel DC path; leakage, noise, mismatch, PVT, finite array loading and standby power remain unqualified. No sense-cell layout or new physical acceptance. All launched runs completed.

Alternatives: (1) non-destructive current read with shared column electronics is the next candidate; (2) local switched-capacitor updates can apply learned beta once per bin, signed weighted accumulation, threshold and subtractive reset in place, but require area/noise evaluation; (3) calibrated destructive read/restore remains a fallback with nonlinear inverse and switch-error burden. Uncontrolled continuous-time leakage is not a substitute for the trained bin equation. A switched-capacitor neuromorphic implementation is documented at https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3233; it establishes precedent, not feasibility for this population.

Next milestone: implement and characterize the sense cell and a real shared column frontend, reduce initial-write error, then integrate one complete analog PLIF neuron preserving the original float model equations. Evaluate model tolerance, 5ms population service and realistic area before full-chip assembly/layout. No QAT/digital fallback. ## MOS state store with ideal state-aware charge — 2026-10-01

An 11-point TT/27°C physical MOS gate bank (100µm² drawn gate area) was calibrated over0.15–1.65V using a0.5fC probe through the physical SKY130 transmission gate. The inferred effective capacitance rises from0.276pF to0.810pF, so a fixed current-to-voltage map cannot cover the state range. Using trapezoidal Q(V) interpolation, ideal signed current pulses then drove the physical bank for actual shuffled event weights from the original epoch58 full-float final-fusion trace. The322-event high-cancellation fan-in occupies17.71µs at55ns slots and stays within19µV of the ideal encoded trajectory at sampled prefixes; its final error is0.16µV. The370-event large-swing fan-in occupies20.35µs and reaches−0.6202V relative to the0.9V center versus−0.6173V target, a−2.87mV endpoint error. Largest ideal pulse current is18.0µA for that large-swing case.

This screen demonstrates that the modeled MOS gate can store both trajectories under externally computed charge; it does not implement the needed state sensor or current source. The branch reference subtraction removes shared programming/hold drift in analysis and is not a circuit. Prefix sampling is sparse; the voltage map and current commands use ideal per-event state knowledge. There is no physical threshold/reset/beta, noise/mismatch, PVT,5ms retention during event processing, extraction, legal layout, energy, or full-population 5ms service result. Thus this result advances the capacitor characterization only. It does not qualify a membrane cell or architecture. Reproduce with `scripts/screen_sky130_mos_state_aware_charge.py`; calibration decks, event decks and logs are under `artifacts/analog_asic/benches/` and `artifacts/analog_asic/results/`. Aggregate report: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_mos_state_aware_ideal_charge_boundary.json`.

## Shared analog weight-buffer prefetch — 2026-09-29

The existing SKY130 transistor OTA, loaded by an injector NMOS gate, was compared at SS/0°C under two ideal input commands in one bounded ngspice deck. At10us the cold branch steps0→0.48V, while the precharged branch steps0.45→0.48V after a10us precharge. The warm output is0.4485V immediately before the step,0.47543V after0.2us,0.48969V after0.5us,0.47855V after2us and0.47874V after3us. The cold output is0.06599V after2us and0.47875V after8us. Thus prefetch substantially reduces this single gate transition, but the warm branch overshoots by9.69mV at0.5us and both branches retain the measured−1.246mV DC error at the0.48V command. This result uses ideal analog command, OTA biases and rail. It has no analog weight storage, mux, calibration, repeated event switching, noise, mismatch, extracted parasitics or complete population schedule. Evidence: `scripts/test_sky130_ms_weight_gate_prefetch.py` and `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_ms_weight_gate_prefetch_ss0_n0p48.json`.

The open-node screen found a real-process55nm candidate, ICsprout55, but its public PDK currently lists SPICE models and RC extraction as unfinished. It is unsuitable for a credible port of this analog cell today. Retain SKY130 circuit evidence while screening newly released physical data. The open 28nm OpenRPDK28 describes itself as under construction; ASAP7 and FreePDK45 are predictive academic processes. Sources: [ICsprout55 repository](https://github.com/openecos-projects/icsprout55-pdk), [OpenRPDK28](https://github.com/RIOSLaboratory/OpenRPDK28), [ASAP7 paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2016.04.006), [FreePDK45](https://eda.ncsu.edu/freepdk/freepdk45/).

## Full-float pulse-duration mapping and service screen — 2026-09-24

The analog reference is `EventSpikeSeg140k_seed17_best.pt`, epoch 58 / best epoch 58 of the 80-epoch run, `is_best=true`, SHA-256 `c934da40b0f65d2a63155cb89b663e06aebf527cea1db4b9902a5b53840457d7`. Exported parameter arrays and sampled software traces use the original float inference path; no QAT, quantized weights, fake quantization or Q7.16-derived values were used. The epoch-80 file is not the best checkpoint and is not the analog reference.

`scripts/analyze_sky130_pulse_float_mapping.py` folds exported ChannelAffine gains into each float convolution weight and compares them with the measured 0.9V SKY130 TT pulse curve (50ns/500us logical width, 7x positive pulse-duration factor). Each layer is independently scaled so its largest effective coefficient fits the largest tested pulse; this is only a sensitivity point, not a selected voltage encoding. The resulting median positive pulse widths are 69us to 306us in sampled stages. Per-layer median learned threshold voltages under those scales range from about 0.23mV (final_fuse) to 4.23mV (stem), illustrating that scale selection alone has not resolved threshold/noise headroom.

For the three recorded real-DSEC patch traces, active convolution inputs were replayed through absolute effective-weight pulse durations. Assuming output neurons operate in parallel but each neuron's incoming contributions serialize, median/p90/p99 service is 0.19/1.64/7.83ms for stem, 2.99/16.81/37.14ms for enc1.standard, and 10.28/48.17/115.39ms for final_fuse.standard. Before setup or settling, 2.28%, 37.98% and 58.79% of active destinations respectively exceed 5ms. This optimistic model shows that one serial pulse lane per postsynaptic membrane does not meet the bin budget for later sampled stages at the max-weight-fit scales. Parallel fan-in, complete-model accuracy and global scheduling remain untested; this result does not prove pulse duration cannot work with a substantially parallel cell array. It is sufficient to start the planned switched-capacitor fallback comparison. ## SKY130 switched-capacitor packet topology screen — 2026-09-24

A first direct-sharing cell uses a PDK MIM packet capacitor, 100µm×100µm MIM membrane and SKY130 CMOS transmission gates. A precharged packet is connected to the membrane for one event; tested packet squares are 10/30/100µm and membrane starts are 0.75/0.90/1.05V. All six sign/size variants transfer in the commanded direction, but absolute packet magnitude is strongly state-dependent. Across the tested states the max/min magnitude ratio is 3.0–4.6×; the 10µm packet's positive magnitude ranges 1.00–4.66mV and the 100µm packet's ranges 74.7–225mV. Thus direct sharing does not implement a fixed signed weighted contribution and is rejected as the standalone cell. This does not reject switched-capacitor injection generally; a bootstrapped/sample-compensated transfer or virtual summing node is next. No weight coding, repeated-event schedule, amplifier, PVT/mismatch, extraction or PLIF acceptance was tested. Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_sc_charge_share.json`, bench `scripts/test_sky130_sc_charge_share.py`.

The MOS virtual-summing-node candidate in `asic/analog/sky130_sc_charge_integrator.spice` uses a two-stage MOS OTA, PDK MIM feedback/packet capacitors, TG packet isolation and a separate TG to reset the isolated packet capacitor between events. The test fixture initially used the wrong MIM initial-condition reference; with the capacitor's differential state initialized as `Vstate−VCM`, the 0.75/0.90/1.05V states are preserved to within 3.14mV before packet injection. With ±0.3V packet steps, 1/3/10µm square capacitors deliver about 32.8µV/0.296mV/3.095mV for positive input and 48.3µV/0.307mV/3.105mV for negative input. Packet variation across the three start states is ≤1.84% at 1µm, ≤0.24% at 3µm, and ≤0.012% at 10µm. Positive/negative gain mismatch is about 47% at 1µm, 3.7% at 3µm and 0.33% at 10µm, so the smallest cap needs a differential switch/offset correction. The inverting topology requires reversing digital sign-to-packet mapping. The sampled virtual-node error is up to 1.74mV. A 90% response-time screen is 3.3–10.9ns after the input step; this excludes switch setup, packet-cap selection/reset and fanout. The 30-case wider sweep exceeded its 60s bound; the completed 18-case sweep covers 1/3/10µm, three states and both signs. Physical initialization, weight-cap selection, bias generation, full PLIF reset, and PVT/mismatch/extraction remain unqualified. Bias rails are ideal, and no float-model spike equivalence is claimed. Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_sc_charge_integrator.json`, bench `scripts/test_sky130_sc_charge_integrator.py`.

The packet capacitor must be isolated from the membrane while its charge is reset. A 12-case two-event sequence screen explicitly separates those phases. At 10µm packet size, the largest error from adding two independently measured packets is 27.14µV; the largest P→N versus N→P order difference is 0.268µV. Absolute cancellation error is ~23–25µV, comparable to or larger than the small residual, so relative cancellation error is not meaningful. Per-event input-to-input spacing is 2.5µs in this provisional schedule, including a break-before-make packet-cap reset phase; this remains a one-cell TT timing screen, not an integrated throughput claim. Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_sc_charge_integrator_accumulation.json`, bench `scripts/test_sky130_sc_charge_integrator_accumulation.py`.

Combining sampled active fan-in counts with a provisional 2.5µs packet cycle (the initial bench action window, not a validated repeating schedule) gives serial per-output service p50/p90/p99/max of 10/45/90/138µs for stem, 120/185/223/275µs for enc1.standard and 530/685/790/925µs for final_fuse.standard. No sampled destination exceeds 5ms under this optimistic dedicated-output assumption. This is a throughput indication only: it omits weight-cap selection, cap reset/precharge, arbitration, restore/ADC and whole-chip routing, and covers three patches from one record. A separate full-float range-to-cap sensitivity maps the final_fuse maximum effective weight to a ~30.5µm capacitor at 0.3V candidate headroom, but its 0.1-percentile weight would require a ~1.4nm square capacitor under linear area extrapolation, below the 1µm smallest tested device. At that same sensitivity scale, the learned threshold is ~10.9µV and the 0.1-percentile candidate-to-threshold margin is ~0.18µV. A uniform 1µV threshold offset changes about 0.28–0.29% of sampled final_fuse spike bits; 10µV changes 1.4–2.5%. These are model sensitivity estimates, not analog noise or mismatch results; small weights may be behaviorally unimportant, but pruning is not authorized. Evidence is included in `sky130_float_pulse_mapping_screen.json`.

## SKY130 Q7.16 restore/mux and writeback controller — 2026-09-23

The current 24-bit R-2R + MIM restore/multiplex schematic smoke passes the **coarse** 3mV rail-window criterion, tested-code monotonicity, and A→B→A round-trip after applying a uniform +12,544-code offset and a +2.553424mV DAC rail shift. The center state is within 46µV of 0.9V; the worst tested error is 2.863mV, or 938.05 declared Q7.16 voltage LSBs; `q716_half_lsb_accuracy_pass=false`. Applying the code offset only to nonnegative codes caused the earlier discontinuity. These are provisional TT schematic corrections, not analog Q7.16 accuracy or ENOB evidence. The 1k/2k values remain ideal and unqualified for physical implementation.

Evidence: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_ms_restore_mux_24bit.json`. The separate 23-bit weight-magnitude voltage-transfer rerun passes its 5mV coarse limit and tested monotonicity on the regenerated 1k/2k ideal ladder; worst tested error is 3.592mV. It does not test MOS injection current or analog precision (`sky130_weight_q716_dac_screen.json`).

The synthesizable SAR/slot controller passed an Icarus Docker RTL smoke: low/offset/full-scale ideal codes yielded expected clipped Q7.16 endpoints over 72 comparator decisions and phase outputs did not overlap. Its decode now inverts the restore path's uniform common-mode code offset. Test source: `scripts/tb_sky130_ms_slot_controller.sv`; RTL: `asic/analog/sky130_ms_slot_controller.sv`; machine report: `artifacts/analog_asic/results/sky130_ms_slot_controller_rtl.json`. Comparator feedback was an ideal code-level model. This is still not an analog-integrated ADC/writeback result; measured restore error remains hundreds of Q7.16 LSBs.

At 30,976,000 membrane identities and 24 sequential SAR decisions per identity, a single lane needs 743,424,000 comparisons per 5ms update. Even at 100MHz this implies at least 1,487 parallel lanes before setup, settle, injection/leak, and routing overhead. This throughput bound blocks any one/few-channel population claim until the architecture is revised or an adequate parallel implementation is demonstrated.

## PDK review — 2026-09-23

Continue with SKY130 for this prototype: the local PDK provides the transistor and MIM models already exercised by the channel/restore benches. IHP SG13G2 is a credible analog/mixed-signal alternative with MIM devices and ngspice support, but IHP labels its open PDK a preview; adopting it would require a fresh model, extraction, and flow qualification. GF180MCU is another open option, but its upstream PDK is also marked experimental preview. A PDK change would not fix the 938-LSB restore precision gap, the direct MOS current-DAC dead zone, or the SAR lane-count lower bound, so the current problems do not justify migration. Sources: [IHP Open PDK](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK), [GF180MCU PDK](https://github.com/google/gf180mcu-pdk).

The old executable 4-bit injector loop was removed from the combined screen.

The original TT operating-point screen (`sky130_weight_q716_injector_screen.json`) tested Q7.16 magnitudes 0, 1, 8, and 68 with both signs and found low-code leakage-floor response and severe sign mismatch. The fresh integrated 1k/2k R-2R/MOS sweep is also unsuitable for weight injection: it remains near cutoff through 25% code, then rises sharply; strict monotonicity fails and full-scale positive/negative current ratio is 0.859. This is DC schematic evidence only, not pulse charge or PLIF accuracy. Keep this direct gate-DAC injector out of acceptance.

Sequential accumulation was screened on a single PDK MIM membrane using the pulse-duration channel: two identical positive events summed to within 0.00045%; mixed positive/negative events in either order were within 0.53% of the independent-pulse sum, and order changed the residual by 0.54%. This supports charge accumulation for the tested TT operating point and event size. It does not establish small-signal linearity, simultaneous events, corners, mismatch, or a weight-code mapping (`sky130_ms_pulse_width_accumulation.json`).

A separate analog injection candidate, `synapse_pulse_width_mos`, keeps the membrane as a capacitor and encodes signed weight by gate-pulse duration. Its full PLIF-channel TT transient screen uses the SKY130 PDK MIM model at 100µm×100µm, and is monotonic across seven logical durations from 0.05 to 4µs. With a 7× longer positive pulse scale, the normalized positive/negative gain ratio is 0.957; worst per-sign slope deviation is 0.36%. A separate single-pulse 5ms hold test on the same channel variant shows 15–18µV drift with leak disabled, passing a provisional 3mV limit. This remains a circuit-level candidate, not Q7.16 weight accuracy: no mismatch, PVT, extracted parasitics, event multiplicity, or population scheduling has been checked. At a hypothetical 100MHz timer, 4µs and 28µs provide only 400 and 2,800 pulse-width ticks (about 8.6 and 11.5 bits of timing levels); the seven-point screen does not establish 24-bit charge precision. The next analog step is to characterize weight-code-to-charge mapping and event accumulation; the restore/writeback DAC monotonicity failure remains a separate blocker.

### Mechanism interpretation

- Adding triangular threshold adaptation to the same v10 family gave a small improvement over PLIF+threshold alone (`0.1459` vs `0.1402`).
- Hidden `winner_peer` inhibition was harmful: its encoder spike rates fell from `0.0474` at enc1 to `0.00306` at enc2 and `0.000149` at enc3, indicating feature starvation.
- Stem-only `peer_membrane` inhibition did not cause that collapse and produced the best mIoU. Its encoder spike rates remained `0.0770`, `0.0363`, and `0.0239`.
- The winning checkpoint learned mean inhibition strength `0.2082`, threshold-adaptation strength `0.1879`, and adaptation duration `5.196`, close to their initial values `0.20`, `0.20`, and `5.0`.
- All five still failed badly on rare classes under this small-data screen. The winner's per-class IoUs were flat `0.4113`, construction+sky `0.7825`, object `0.0006`, nature `0`, human `0`, vehicle `0`.

Because this run used only 256 training samples, it is used to choose neuron dynamics, not to replace the full-budget `v10_fpga_hybrid` incumbent.

## Reproducibility note

The top-ten, top-five, and top-three registries are all trained through `eventspikeseg.train`. Historical suites are pinned to the objective used for the recorded architecture-search results (`0.5 CE + 0.5 focal + 0.75 Dice`, plus historical auxiliary supervision). The final suite keeps total CE coefficient 1.0 but dynamically transfers weight from pixel CE to equal target-present-class macro CE, ramps Dice/boundary supervision up, and ramps auxiliary CE down by completed epoch fraction. Validation-on-train-holdout best-checkpoint selection and the canonical refinement schedule remain active. The old standalone `benchmark_top_three.py` runner is retired; its unique protocol has been represented in the shared trainer/launch configuration.

has arrived. Therefore, the longest dependency-path sum of configured-bank commit costs is a
response-latency lower bound even though current collection can overlap upstream activity. On the
1,718-lane throughput configuration this floor is 1,050,545 cycles (10.796 ms at 97.31 MHz), so
that configuration cannot meet a 5 ms single-bin response deadline.

## Capacitor-only readout and OTA sensitivity — 2026-09-25

Tested a passive MIM differential sampler as an alternative to the ideal 1GΩ OTA readout (`scripts/test_sky130_sc_cap_differential_sample.py`). In the 10µm case (203.8fF estimated from typical SKY130 MIM area/perimeter density), the bottom-plate sequence disturbs the membrane differential by 2.5–3.9µV during the 100µs sample/hold window. The output includes a large nominal feedthrough offset (about −0.466mV in the no-event case); a VCM-only dummy does not cancel it within a run. Across four packet orders, subtracting a separate no-event simulator control from the paired real-minus-dummy reading recovers the corresponding state change to 0.05–0.09µV at TT. This is only an offline control subtraction, not an implemented baseline circuit. A smaller 1µm sampler shows severe feedthrough (about −27.1mV) and is rejected. At 30µm (1.811pF estimate), the `pp` output/control delta agrees with the state delta within 0.14µV, with an 8.1µV differential disturbance; however, its estimated kT/C voltage scale at 300K is still 47.8µV RMS, close to the ~55µV two-packet signal. The 10µm kT/C scale is 142.6µV RMS, above the signal. These are thermal-noise estimates, not simulated transient-noise results; larger caps reduce this noise but increase membrane loading. Passive sampling is not accepted as a low-noise solution.

A direct OTA input-sensing screen (`scripts/test_sky130_sc_ota_diff_sensitivity.py`) avoids a passive sampling capacitor at the input. With the present 10/20/4µm input stage and tuned 2/27.8µm second stage, a ±64µV differential at 0.9V common mode moves the output by −314/+323mV (incremental gain about −4.9k to −5.0k V/V). At ±250µV the output approaches 0.18/1.70V and is strongly nonlinear; this is a high-gain detector, not a linear state readout. Next tune a closed-loop or time-integrating differential readout for useful range and offset handling, then characterize its noise and corners. Evidence: `results/sky130_sc_cap_differential_sample_{pp,nn,pn,np,zero}_10p0um_bp.json`, corresponding `.dat` waveforms, `results/sky130_sc_cap_differential_sample_{pp,zero}_30p0um_bp.json`, and `results/sky130_sc_ota_diff_sensitivity.json`.

### Late OTA comparator timestep and event-order follow-up — 2026-09-25

The minimum-width (`win=0.5µm`) late-switched OTA comparator was rechecked at a 10ns maximum timestep with input-gate precharge set to the measured 5ns membrane common mode (0.8882V), rather than accepting the earlier optimistic 100ns result. In `pp`/`nn` same-sign cases, the comparator-minus-matched-reference output has the correct state sign and membrane differential disturbance is −0.158/−0.190µV. In mixed `pn`/`np` cases, disturbances are −0.170/−0.172µV, but the near-zero `np` state (−1.953µV at comparison) is reported positive: output difference is +6.162mV. `pn` (state +1.634µV) is reported positive with +6.848mV output difference. Thus the current paired-reference comparator does not reliably resolve the mixed residual; a millivolt-level output baseline difference dominates the sign, while the sampled state kick is itself close to the previously inferred ~0.18µV full-float sensitivity margin. The apparent near-zero disturbance at 100ns did not reproduce at finer timesteps. Evidence: `results/sky130_sc_ota_plif_comparator_{pp,nn,pn,np}_w0.5_t1.5us_p0p8882_s10n.json` and `scripts/test_sky130_sc_ota_plif_comparator.py`.

This blocks the present direct late-sampling comparator, not the SC integration path. Continue with an explicit threshold/reference and offset-zeroing phase, seeking a decision margin at the learned float threshold while keeping membrane kick below its measured error budget. Then use a fast representative integration-window test, event-order replay and full-float sensitivity before corner/mismatch work. These results are nominal TT schematic evidence only: no device mismatch, transient noise, extracted parasitics or physical layout qualification.

### Buffered threshold readout and matched-baseline calibration — 2026-09-25

The direct late OTA sign comparator and direct threshold-shifted comparator were not reliable at 10ns; mixed `np` was wrong-sign even after a +10.9µV reference shift. A different readout was tested while preserving the switched-capacitor membrane integrator: late-connect the two held membrane outputs to separate unity-feedback OTA buffers, then use a physical SKY130 xhigh-poly feedback OTA and a matched same-common-mode baseline OTA. Open the membrane sample transmission gate before reconnecting the gate precharge (100ns nonoverlap) and keep OTA bias on across that interval. This phase ordering reduced the mixed-state membrane kick and isolates feedback resistors from the membrane nodes.

At a 10ns timestep, with the reference membrane initialized +10.9µV above the signal cell (the prior median final-fusion threshold estimate at 0.30V candidate headroom), gain trim 10.1, and 1MΩ/approximately 9.1MΩ xhigh-poly feedback network, the two mixed orders both remain below threshold and have the correct baseline-subtracted output sign:

| order | differential before readout (µV) | at comparison (µV) | after (µV) | readout relation error (µV out) | input-equivalent error (µV) | decision |

### Membrane MIM area and noise correction (2026-09-25)

The earlier 100 um square capacitor area figure was a SPICE bench scenario scaled to all 30,976,000 logical PLIF states; it was not a selected cell size. Likewise, the 0.18 uV point came from local final-fusion spike sensitivity and is not a specified capacitor kT/C requirement. Those assumptions overstated the implication that an analog MIM state array must exceed memory area.

Using the measured 10 um MIM value (203.8 fF) as an area-density estimate (~2.038 fF/um2), simple one-cap-per-state scenarios are: 1 um squares: ~31.0 mm2 total and ~1.43 mV kT/C; 10 um squares: ~3,098 mm2 and ~143 uV; 100 um squares: ~309,760 mm2 and ~14.3 uV. These are geometric/noise scenarios only; 1 um may not satisfy PDK minimum geometry, and switches, routing, guards, peripheral circuits, and layout spacing are excluded. The 100 um point is only the existing bench cap.

Conclusion: MIM area can indeed be well below a same-capacity digital state implementation. Area alone does not rule out analog membrane storage. The unresolved engineering question is whether a realizable smaller capacitor plus circuit noise, leakage, event charge, restore, and readout preserves full-float network behavior. The local 0.18 uV sensitivity result must not be used as a universal kT/C requirement or as an area floor.

### SKY130 MIM geometry and packet-resolution screen (2026-09-25)

Read the local SKY130 model (`cap_mim_m3_2`): nominal typical parameters are `camimc=2.00 fF/um2` and `cpmimc=0.19 fF/um`. For a square width w, the model is approximately C=2.00w^2+0.76w fF (before process offsets). The shipped 1um model test gives 2.642 fF. One MIM per each of 30,976,000 logical states would occupy 30.976 mm2 at 1um squares, 3,097.6 mm2 at 10um, 12,390.4 mm2 at 20um, 77,440 mm2 at 50um, and 309,760 mm2 at 100um, excluding all other layout. Thus the earlier 100um bench assumption is much too pessimistic for raw capacitor area; the 1um scenario is materially smaller, although a true physical density comparison with same-capacity SRAM still needs matched macros and layout overhead.

The area benefit creates a packet-resolution issue. The existing passive cell uses a 1um packet MIM and 0.3V top-plate steps to produce about 41uV on a 100um state MIM. Preserving that step under ideal capacitive scaling would require roughly 75mV with a 50um state cap, 3mV with 10um, and 0.08mV with 1um, using the same 1um packet. The smallest-state cases therefore need a much smaller packet capacitor, a low-noise fine analog pulse source, or another charge scaling method. This is a design tradeoff, not evidence that the large membrane cap is required.

Thus simply shortening the pulse does not restore linear accumulation over a meaningful event count. A nominal saturation-bias gate level (pMOS 1.2V, nMOS 0.6V) also failed to improve 100-event accumulation: +160.96/+143.30mV versus isolated-pulse linear extrapolations +1.952/+1.768V, ≈92% short. Doubling injector length to 20µm changed the same-sign response by little (≈158/178mV vs ≈1.94/1.99V extrapolated); adding 1MΩ source degeneration also did not materially improve it (≈161/163mV vs ≈1.95/1.91V). This variant still lacks a separate regulated current-source device and cannot be called a proper current source; the drive gate level merely changes the injector MOS operating point. A trial shrinking transistor width below the SKY130 model's valid bin produced no valid device model and was rejected as a simulation, not a circuit result. The next useful current-injection experiment needs explicit current bias plus pulse steering and a separate off switch, keeping device sizes within the model range; compare state dependence over the actual float event distribution. The 2ns logical pulse is currently a transient-time-resolution screen, not a feasible 5ms scheduler or extracted timing result.

## 2026-09-25 — differential MIM integration reduces single-ended compression

Added `scripts/test_sky130_ms_diff_current_many_events.py`: two matched 20µm MIM capacitors start at 0.9V, and signed events steer complementary pMOS-source/nMOS-sink currents so the nodes move in opposite directions. A no-event pair stays matched and drifts about 0.147mV over 5ms. At TT, 10µm injector length, pMOS gate=0.72V, nMOS gate=0.60V and 10.5ns physical pulse width, one event changes the differential by 1.873mV with only 0.034mV common-mode shift. In a 100-event equal-sign train, differential change is 173.97mV versus 187.28mV from the isolated event (7.1% low); common mode moves −2.98mV relative to the no-event pair. An alternating 50/50-sign train leaves −2.69mV differential residual and −3.08mV common-mode shift. At 7ns the same circuit is 23.7% high after 100 events; at 14ns it is 17.8% low. Thus differential storage improves greatly over the single-ended 90%+ compression, but still has pulse-width/state nonlinearity, polarity-order residual, common-mode motion and unqualified PVT/mismatch. Bias values and width are one-point nominal TT calibration only. The test uses direct MOS gates, no explicit reference-current mirror, read amplifier, threshold, reset/leak, physical layout or network feedback; it is a promising topology screen, not an accepted circuit.

Additional equal-charge stress: the same pMOS/nMOS biases and 10.5ns pulses were run at 316 events (the sampled final-fuse p99 active-destination fan-in) and 370 events (the sampled maximum), spread across the 5ms interval. The 316-event same-sign differential change was 608.21mV versus 592.28mV extrapolated (+2.69%); alternating 158/158 signs left +0.183mV differential residual. At 370 events the change was 700.47mV versus 693.48mV extrapolated (+1.01%); alternating signs left −0.423mV residual. Same-sign final node voltages were 1.197/0.589V at 316 and 1.241/0.541V at 370; common mode shifted −6.90/−8.84mV relative to the no-event reference. These are equal-width same-sign stress trains, not the model's mixed signed weight/activity sequence, so they do not qualify transfer accuracy. Reverse alternating order at 100 events flips the residual from −2.687mV to +2.687mV, identifying event-order nonlinearity rather than a static sign offset. Results: `sky130_ms_diff_current_many_events_n100_*` and `n316_*`/`n370_*` in `artifacts/analog_asic/results/`.

Burst timing screen: 370 events were also packed 15ns apart with 10.5ns pulse width, completing in about 5.55µs inside the same 5ms bin. Same-sign differential change was 585.11mV versus 587.19mV linear expectation (0.35% low), with final nodes 1.188/0.603V. A 185/185 alternating train left 0.108mV differential residual. This shows the gate pulses can be serviced far faster than the earlier passive packet cycle in this schematic, though event-width resolution, control distribution and actual weighted event timing remain unqualified.

The follow-up explicit current-source plus TG-steering variant is not the lead. With one-stage ordinary switches it drifted about0.20V in the no-event 5ms reference; two-stage long-channel switches reduced reference drift to about4µV, but charge injection/current during one 14ns pulse produced excessive differential steps (about0.62V with 10/20µm TGs, about59mV with 1/2µm TGs) and large common-mode shifts. Lengthening the current-source devices to50µm did not improve the one-pulse transfer (about85mV). Thus the separate-source TG topology remains a failed schematic attempt; retain the direct differential MOS injector as the current leading candidate for full-float mapping. Results/logs: `sky130_ms_diff_steered_current_*`.

### Fixed-width MOS gate-amplitude mapping and weighted event sequence — 2026-09-25

The direct differential MOS injector was extended with a fixed 10.5 ns pulse whose pMOS/nMOS gate magnitude carries each full-float weight. Gate transfer is calibrated using the SKY130 TT devices and a matched 20 µm MIM pair. Directly measuring `v(vp)-v(vn)` avoids the 0.1 µV quantization created by subtracting separately printed ~0.9 V node voltages. The calibration transient uses a 0.5 ns maximum step and initializes both the external MIM nodes and each model's internal series-resistance capacitor plate to VCM; outer-node initialization alone leaves the internal capacitor state inconsistent and invalidates that earlier sweep/sequence. With corrected initialization, a maximum-strength isolated event changes the differential by 1.596 mV and common mode by about −6.8 µV at the end of a 200 µs screen.

Using that measured curve to map the full-float `final_fuse.standard` coefficients, no weights exceed the measured transfer range at 0.30 V candidate headroom; 0.017% of static coefficients are below the lowest tested gate fraction. An ideal continuous gate map gives 0.00051% local spike-bit mismatch on the three frozen DSEC patches. Uniform 12-bit gate-fraction coding gives 0.0111% mismatch. These are ideal digital-code replay estimates, not a built gate DAC or programmed analog weight storage; there is no noise, mismatch, PVT, extraction, full-network or task-accuracy evidence.

A representative maximum-fan-in location from the recorded full-float presynaptic tensor expands to 370 weighted events and a −17.485 mV target at this scale. Events spread uniformly across 5 ms and mapped through the single-event curve produce −17.256 mV in negative-first order, −18.079 mV in reverse order and −18.578 mV in one deterministic shuffled order. Forward/reverse order differs by 0.823 mV, while shuffled total-charge error is −6.25%. The differential-pair common mode ends near 0.906 V in these 10.5 ns runs. This demonstrates that isolated-event calibration is not enough for full-float accumulation; the current cell is not accepted.

A fixed 128 ns pulse made the same weighted sequence worse: shuffled output −2.964 mV and reverse output −25.110 mV versus −17.485 mV target, with 22.0 mV order spread. The run's JSON inherited an old scope sentence saying 10.5 ns; its actual deck used 128 ns. A scaled long-channel device (`Wp=4.5 µm`, `Wn=3 µm`, `L=30 µm`) also failed: shuffled output −11.939 mV (31.7% error), reverse/forward span 37.45 mV, and common mode near 1.03 V. Retain the `L=10 µm`, 10.5 ns direct differential injector as the best current branch, but keep it provisional. Next compare a 10 µm MIM pair to test a lower-area state capacitor under the same full-float weighted sequence, then investigate current-source/common-mode regulation if transfer still varies with membrane state. Do not use QAT or the quantized export.

The direct MOS branch remains provisional and also order-sensitive; do not infer the real network's event ordering from the binned traces. Next characterize several randomized within-bin orders and investigate measured-state compensation on the MOS lead, while preserving this passive result as a failed fallback screen. Retain fixed-width presynaptic event pulses and encode signed weight in the analog injected-current/charge amplitude. A bounded SS/0°C sample-and-hold bench programs two physical SKY130 MIM capacitors through TGs to the p/n injector gate levels, holds them, then applies one40.253ns positive event to a10µm first-touch membrane pair. Directly switching a10µm stored gate capacitor onto the MOS gate causes large charge sharing: after a short hold the stored p/n nodes move about+122/−47mV during the event, and the delivered differential is101.61µV versus408.94µV with ideal direct drive. After5ms, the programmed p/n levels have drifted−2.984/+38.624mV before connection. A20µm pair reduces but does not remove this error. With a100µm pair and a longer10µs programming window,5ms drift is−0.033/+0.420mV, yet the event still differs from direct drive by−11.87µV (−2.90%). The1µs programming window used in the first100µm run was too short; only the10µs result is used for its area/error comparison.

The alternative holds the weight capacitors continuously on the MOS gates and steers current at the drains. With idle drain nodes clamped to rails, a gate-off event switch still moves the membrane differential≈21.93mV, compared with≈3.19mV of gate-dependent contribution at fraction0.5. Clamping the idle drain nodes to VCM reduces the gate-off switching contribution to≈0.351µV and the ideal gate-dependent contribution to≈2.837µV, but produces continuous idle current (the four-cell comparison bench draws≈1.9µA from its shared1.8V supply just before the event; this cannot be divided into a validated per-weight power figure). After5ms at fraction0.5, the gate-dependent contribution is+91% over the ideal-gate value with a10µm pair, +20% with20µm, +3.1% with50µm and +0.77% with100µm. The corresponding bare two-cap areas across folded PLIF weights are28.75,114.98,718.64 and2,874.56mm². At10µm, hold intervals100/500/1000µs give approximately−5.0/+0.7/+8.4% error relative to an ideal-gate event; the nonmonotonic result includes programming offset and cannot justify a simple500µs refresh schedule. This is a deterministic one-weight, one-event schematic screen without thermal noise, local mismatch, refresh hardware, many-weight mapping, full-fanin accumulation, readout or extraction.
